newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Talks planned on strike at Moscow's Bykovo airport.
newsitem.headline: Talks planned on strike at Moscow's Bykovo airport.

text.p: Air traffic controllers plan to begin talks with Federal Aviation Service (FAS) officials in an effort to end a strike paralysing Moscow's Bykovo domestic airport for a third day, a strike committee official said on Friday.
"We will begin talks with the FAS on Saturday," the official told Reuters by telephone.
He said strikers were ready for compromise, but gave no further details.
He also said controllers had allowed only two out of 80 regular and charter flights to leave Bykovo since the strike began. These were flights carrying heads of Russian regions.
Air traffic controllers have been striking for higher salaries and benefits from October 23. Earlier this week a strike leader said the FAS had refused to meet strikers demands.
Bykovo, one of four Moscow airports, has no international flights. It operates regular and charter flights to 25 destinations in central Russia, the Urals and Siberia.
